transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-20
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Samira Patel (Redwood SE), Maya Chen (Halo Head of Partnerships), Diego Alvarez (Halo Sales Director), Priya Rao (Halo Solutions Architect)
Recorder: Fireflies.ai
Meeting id: ffx-2026-12-20-halo-001

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh we should be recording this -- hi Maya, Diego, Priya, thanks for making time. Quick agenda, pipeline review, tech blockers, and next steps for the co-sell pilot.

[00:17] Maya Chen: Yep thanks Jordan, yeah excited to sync. We sent the list of deals earlier this week, hope you had a chance to look.

[00:26] Jordan Lee: I skimmed it, thanks. We'll walk through top three. Samira, do you want to kick off on the technical side?

[00:33] Samira Patel: Sure. So for the pilot we saw three main models of integration from Halo: 1) hosted API calls from your app to Redwood hosted endpoints, 2) dedicated capacity for high throughput customers, and 3) private deployment inside Halo's VPC for regulated accounts. We looked at the sample workloads and there's a mix of long chat sessions and short prompt generation. Latency targets look like sub-400ms 95p for the short calls and under 2s for the long chat flows, which is doable depending on batching and model choice.

[01:10] Priya Rao: Quick question, when you say "dedicated capacity" is that the Redwood Dedicated offering? And does that include a private control plane or is that only for the Private product?

[01:20] Samira Patel: Good callout. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with isolated capacity and SLA - it still uses Redwood control plane but we can restrict data flows. Private is the fully customer-managed control plane option – VPC peered or on-prem. For Halo's larger regulated deals we recommend Private or a VPC option, but Dedicated can be fine for predictable throughput where data residency isn't strict.

[01:44] Diego Alvarez: From a sales perspective, most of our top targets are asking for SOC 2 and SSO/SAML, also KMS integration for key management. Is that covered?

[01:54] Jordan Lee: Absolutely. Redwood has SOC 2 Type II, SAML SSO, RBAC, and we support KMS integrations/HSM for private key management. We'll attach the security pack. I will re-share the SOC2 attestation and the security brief after this call.

[02:09] Maya Chen: Perfect. On the list of deals, we flagged Acme Health, LuminaPay, and Origen Retail as the best candidates. Acme wants a private deployment, LuminaPay is open to Dedicated, Origen is more of a hosted/skunkworks test. Any concerns there?

[02:30] Samira Patel: Acme's private deployment is the most complex – Priya, could you share the network/topology constraints?

[02:36] Priya Rao: Sure, Acme requires no outbound internet from their inference cluster, strict IP allowlists, and quarterly audits. They also want per-tenant keys. We can do a behind-the-firewall deployment but need Redwood to support air-gapped install or an on-prem package.

[02:56] Samira Patel: We do have an on-prem package, but full air-gap installs add time. If Acme agrees to a VPC peering model with private subnets and a customer-managed KMS, we can move faster. Otherwise, the on-prem route will add 6-8 weeks just for infra validation.

[03:18] Diego Alvarez: That timeline might push their procurement window. So for quoting we should account for the extra integration mgmt.

[03:25] Jordan Lee: Good note. For pipeline positioning, we should classify Acme as "enterprise - private deployment" and mark expected close Q2. LuminaPay looks like Q1 if Dedicated slots are available.

[03:39] Maya Chen: About the Dedicated slots - how much lead time do we need to reserve GPUs? We don't want to promise customers something we can't deliver.

[03:47] Samira Patel: For Dedicated, typically 2-3 weeks to provision and test if it's a standard N-series GPU pool. If they need a specific quantized profile or custom kernels, add another week. For very large throughput, we'd recommend reserved capacity with a monthly commit.

[04:06] Maya Chen: Understood. On the commercial front, Halo will own first-line relationship but we want clear co-sell motions. Who owns which parts of the pitch and how are commissions handled?

[04:18] Jordan Lee: We usually do a shared-capture model: Halo leads intro and initial meetings, Redwood supports with technical deep dives and benchmarks. For pilot deals we suggest a joint proof-of-performance where Redwood provides discounted pilot credits and Halo covers customer engagement. We'll formalize commission splits in the MSA. I can share a draft MSA and co-sell playbook.

[04:40] Diego Alvarez: Cool. Could you share a sample playbook now? Even a one-pager would help our reps.

[04:46] Jordan Lee: Yes, I'll send.

[04:48] Samira Patel: Tech note: for the benchmark we need a representative sample dataset and a few traffic profiles. Priya, can Halo provide a sanitized sample and target QPS for LuminaPay and Origen?

[05:01] Priya Rao: Yes LuminaPay can provide a masked dataset, approx 200 QPS-ish for peak. Origen is low volume, maybe 10 QPS. I'll coordinate with their infra team to prepare a sanitized bundle.

[05:13] Jordan Lee: Great. Samira – what's the benchmark plan? End-to-end? Latency and cost per 1M tokens?

[05:21] Samira Patel: We'll run end-to-end tests from Halo's network where possible; measure 50/95/99 latencies, throughput, and CPU/GPU utilization. We'll also estimate token cost at different batching configs and provide recommendations: e.g., use smaller context model for short prompts, and larger with kv-cache optimizations for chat. We'll deliver a spreadsheet with results.

[05:44] Maya Chen: Any dependencies on our side for the benchmark – SSH keys, peering, or sample traffic?

[05:50] Samira Patel: If we're testing Hosted variants, minimal. For Dedicated or Private, we'll need temporary access to a test VPC or peering. We'll document steps in the runbook.

[06:02] Diego Alvarez: Also want to surface one of the competitive concerns: several customers ask about model governance and ability to control prompt injection. How do we address that?

[06:12] Samira Patel: We offer prompt validation hooks, content filters, and a policy engine. It's not perfect – sometimes transcription labels it as "policy" – but we can set up guardrails and monitoring. We can also run evals on your prompt set to detect drift.

[06:29] Maya Chen: Good. Back to pilots – who signs the MSA and who needs to be looped in on our side?

[06:35] Jordan Lee: For co-sell pilots we typically have a simple SOW under the MSA. Jordan (AE) will own commercial terms, and our Legal will coordinate with Halo legal. We'll need an exec sponsor from Halo (Maya offered) and an internal Redwood sponsor (I'll be that).

[06:50] Maya Chen: Happy to be sponsor. We'll push to get the deals list and contacts by Thursday.

[06:57] Priya Rao: Quick technical ask: LuminaPay does PCI-adjacent work – do you support tokenization and not storing PII in logs?

[07:06] Samira Patel: Yes you can disable logging for sensitive fields, and we support tokenization patterns. For full PCI scope we recommend Private deployment with customer-managed logging and KMS so nothing persists in Redwood-managed logs.

[07:25] Diego Alvarez: On the topic of pricing, what's the pilot pricing model? Flat fee or per-token?

[07:31] Jordan Lee: Pilots typically have a discounted per-token rate plus a small setup fee if private infra is required. For Dedicated pilots sometimes it's a monthly pilot capacity charge. We'll propose specific numbers in the quote.

[07:43] Maya Chen: Can you give us a ballpark for Dedicated per-month? Diego is asking for budgeting only.

[07:48] Jordan Lee: Ballpark – depends on GPU profile. A modest Dedicated pool for small customers could be in the mid five-figures per month; enterprise workloads scale up. I'll add ranges in the playbook.

[08:00] Priya Rao: Also, do you offer a fallback policy if a model variant is unavailable? For resilience in production.

[08:06] Samira Patel: Yes, the runtime has smart routing and automatic fallback to compatible model variants or spill to lower-cost pools. We'll configure SLO-based fallbacks in the rollout policy.

[08:19] Maya Chen: Great. Anything else tech we should know before the benchmark?

[08:24] Samira Patel: One more: quantization profiles. If you need to hit latency/cost targets we can recommend INT8 or other quantized variants, but there can be small quality differences – we'll include quality checks in the run.

[08:38] Diego Alvarez: Competitor question – a few customers have asked us to compare to CloudCo's managed endpoints. How is Redwood differentiated on 95p latency and cost?

[08:47] Jordan Lee: Two quick differentiators: first, we focus on production economics with tooling to tune batching/caching and runtime kernels to reduce per-token cost; second, unified deployment modes (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) with the same API and rollout tools. We'll share a benchmarking doc comparing to CloudCo and VertexAI – it's not perfect apples-to-apples but helpful.

[09:06] Maya Chen: Good. Let's talk timeline: when can we expect the benchmark and the draft MSA?

[09:12] Jordan Lee: I can get the playbook and draft MSA to you by 2027-01-05. Samira can start benchmarks as soon as we get sanitized sample data – target deliverable by 2026-12-28.

[09:25] Priya Rao: I'll aim to have sample data and network contacts by 2026-12-22.

[09:30] Diego Alvarez: Sounds like a plan. One more sales ops question: do you have a joint logo/co-marketing package for pilots? We like to show partnership in customer-facing materials.

[09:39] Jordan Lee: Yes we have a one-pager co-marketing kit and case study template. I'll include that in the playbook.

[09:45] Maya Chen: Awesome. Anything outstanding from Redwood side?

[09:49] Samira Patel: Nothing else technical right now – just need the sample and a confirmation of the target QPS and latency SLOs per deal.

[09:58] Jordan Lee: Great. Quick recap for notes: Jordan will send playbook, draft MSA, and security pack by 2027-01-05. Samira will run benchmarks once sample data is in and deliver results by 2026-12-28. Maya will provide three target deals and sanitized data by 2026-12-22. We'll schedule an exec intro week of 2026-12-27.

[10:26] Maya Chen: Confirmed. Thanks everyone.

[10:30] Jordan Lee: Thanks all. We'll follow up with calendar invites and docs. Bye.

End of transcript.
